action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. Apply it carefully for now: Bitcoin fell about 5% in a day alongside a sharp drop in US tech stocks, has been under its 50-day average for 16 days (about 7% below it), the mood reads fear at 28 out of 100, and price is only about 4% above its 200-day average of $73,200. So keep any increase small and easy to pause, lead with trust, safety and explainer messages, speed up only once price closes back above about $82,011, and pause the increase if price closes below $73,200. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($76,234) is about 4% above its 200-day average ($73,200), which is still rising.
Up about 17% over 90 days; about 89% of those days closed above the long-term average.

watch: Bitcoin is now only about 4% above its 200-day average, while many people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can speed up a fall if price slips. A close below $73,200 would put the long-run uptrend in question, while a close back above $78,250 would ease the pressure.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but a global tech-stock sell-off pulled Bitcoin about 5% lower in a day, so the short term is soft to neutral. At about $76,234, Bitcoin has now closed under its 50-day average for 16 days, sits about 7% below it and about 9% under its 30-day high, and the Fear & Greed reading has slipped to 28, which is fear. News is taking a little more off the week: the Nasdaq fell 5.5% as AI-related shares slumped, and researchers report an iPhone flaw that has drained about $5.57M from crypto wallets (both PANews). A normal week swings about $3,971, so a close above $78,250 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $74,250 (bottom of a typical week's swing) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; for the bigger picture, $73,200 (the 200-day average) is the floor. Calmer stock markets would steady the week, while a slide under $74,250 is the cue for safety-first messaging.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 17% higher and about 89% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 8.5% and a lot of people are still betting on a rise with borrowed money, which can make any further dip sharper. Price must win back $82,011 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. On the news side, reports say the main US crypto rules bill may now stay stalled until 2028 after the Democratic win in Congress (CNBC via PANews), and the next Fed meeting is on 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for a reclaim of that average.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 4% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 4% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 39% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,200 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,463 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Long-run news roughly balances out, with Europe's largest fund manager Amundi putting fund shares on Ethereum and Greece passing a 10% tax on crypto gains (PANews); a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.why: PANews reports the Nasdaq fell 5.5% as AI-related chip and data-center shares slumped, with South Korea's main index down over 8% and Japan's over 5% the next morning. Crypto fell across the board, with the DePIN group down over 7% and crypto-linked shares such as Circle and BitMine down nearly 10%. AI-themed tokens fell harder than Bitcoin; the reports give no separate reason beyond the wider sell-off.
items.marketing_angle: A plain explainer on why crypto often moves with tech stocks fits today; avoid any 'buy the dip' framing.

items.why: Security researchers report an iPhone flaw kit called DarkSword that steals wallet keys when users open infected websites, with about $5.57M lost so far; CZ urged users to update their phones. Floki took its trading bot offline to investigate an exploit, and SignalPlus said a network attack cost under $82,000 and users will be fully repaid, after Binance removed its connection keys.
items.marketing_angle: Good timing for safety education: phone updates, recovery phrases and connected-app permissions.
